question.name: CSEC Bio May 2023 Q1c(i) — Structural Differences Between Cell Types
question.text:
Complete Table 2 to show ONE structural difference between each pair of cells listed.

Cell PairStructural Difference
Red blood cell vs. Skin cell[[1]]
Skin cell vs. Nerve cell[[2]]
question.general_feedback:
Structural differences between cell types:

Cell PairStructural Difference
Red blood cell vs. Skin (epidermal) cellThe red blood cell has no nucleus (anucleate); the skin cell has a nucleus. The RBC loses its nucleus during maturation to make more room for haemoglobin and to maximise oxygen-carrying capacity.
Skin (epidermal) cell vs. Nerve cellThe skin cell is compact/flat (polygonal shape); the nerve cell is elongated, with a long axon (sometimes over 1 metre long) for transmitting electrical impulses over long distances. Nerve cells also have dendrites for receiving impulses.

steps.label: Compare structural features: nucleus presence/absence; shape; organelles; adaptations
State ONE structural difference between a red blood cell and a skin cell. (2 marks)
State ONE structural difference between a skin cell and a nerve cell. (2 marks)

fields.label: ONE structural difference between a red blood cell and a skin cell:
fields.expected: Red blood cell has no nucleus; skin cell has a nucleus
fields.diagnostic_hint: The most important structural difference is: the red blood cell has NO nucleus (it is anucleate), while the skin cell has a nucleus. A secondary acceptable answer is shape: RBC is biconcave disc vs. compact/polygonal skin cell.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) lose their nucleus during maturation. This makes them anucleate (no nucleus). Skin (epidermal) cells are normal eukaryotic cells with a nucleus. This is the most prominent structural difference between these two cell types.

options.Red blood cell has no nucleus; skin cell: Red blood cell has no nucleus; skin cell has a nucleus
options.Red blood cell is larger than the skin c: Red blood cell is larger than the skin cell
options.Red blood cell has a cell wall; skin cel: Red blood cell has a cell wall; skin cell does not

fields.label: ONE structural difference between a skin cell and a nerve cell:
fields.expected: Nerve cell is elongated with a long axon; skin cell is compact
fields.diagnostic_hint: The nerve cell is elongated with a long axon (for conducting electrical impulses) and dendrites. The skin cell is compact/flat (polygonal). The key structural difference is the long axon of the nerve cell.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Nerve cells (neurones) are adapted for conducting electrical impulses over long distances. They have a long fibre called an axon (which can be over 1 metre long) and branched extensions called dendrites. Skin (epidermal) cells are compact and polygonal in shape, with no long extensions.

options.Nerve cell is elongated with a long axon: Nerve cell is elongated with a long axon; skin cell is compact
options.Nerve cell is smaller than the skin cell: Nerve cell is smaller than the skin cell
options.Nerve cell has a cell wall; skin cell do: Nerve cell has a cell wall; skin cell does not
